items.title: Every One of Mississauga's Cheapest August Home Sales Was a Condo, Zoocasa Finds
items.summary: According to INsauga, the least expensive home sold in Mississauga last month went for $309,000, according to a Zoocasa analysis of Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data. The outlet reports every one of the least expensive homes sold in August was a condo apartment. INsauga reports the average price for a condo apartment in Mississauga fell to $495,052 in August, down from $511,649 in July and from $549,936 in August 2025. According to the outlet, one of the least expensive sales was a three-bedroom, two-storey condo in Sheridan near the QEW and Clarkson GO Station, which sold for $400,000, above its $384,900 list price. INsauga reports another was an updated one-bedroom condo in City Centre featuring floor-to-ceiling windows, stainless steel appliances and a parking space with a locker.

items.title: Mulaney Says Festival's Postponement Wasn't His Call, Plans Return to the Region Soon
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, comedian John Mulaney says he intends to perform in the Mississauga region soon after the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival he was set to headline was postponed at the last minute. The outlet reports the festival, scheduled to run at Erindale Park from Friday to Sunday, was called off in an Instagram post from organizers on Tuesday. According to the Star, organizers wrote that postponing the show was the right decision to ensure they could deliver the best possible festival, even though they knew there was a lot of excitement around it. The outlet reports Mulaney posted on social media Tuesday night saying the decision to move the festival's dates was not his. According to the Star, organizers are exploring new dates and plan to follow up directly with ticket holders.

items.title: GoFundMe Details Long Road Ahead for Amherst Father and Son After Highway 403 Crash
items.summary: According to INsauga, a father and son from the Buffalo area are facing life-altering injuries after a multi-vehicle crash on Highway 403 in Mississauga last month. The outlet reports 43-year-old Masud Biswas has lost both legs above the knee, while his 12-year-old son Marif has already undergone about half a dozen surgeries and could need dozens more as doctors try to save his legs. INsauga reports Ontario Provincial Police said the Amherst, New York family was returning home from Toronto on August 11 when the crash occurred, and both were initially reported to have suffered critical, life-threatening injuries. According to the outlet, a GoFundMe campaign set up by the family's neighbours says Masud remains hospitalized in Ontario in stable condition, while Marif has been transferred to Golisano Children's Hospital in Buffalo, also in stable condition. INsauga reports Marif, a seventh-grade student at Amherst Middle School who enjoyed soccer and basketball before the crash, has been passing the time in hospital building Lego sets.

items.title: Erindale Park Comedy Festival Debut Called Off Days Before Opening Night
items.summary: According to INsauga, the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival has been called off just days before it was set to debut at Mississauga's Erindale Park. The outlet reports Ward 7 Councillor Dipika Damerla announced the cancellation on social media Tuesday, saying organizers made the difficult decision to postpone the September 11 to 13 event. INsauga reports organizers did not give a specific reason for the postponement, saying in a statement that delivering the best possible festival was their priority and that they are exploring new dates. According to the outlet, the festival had been expected to draw roughly 12,500 people to each of its five shows, with a lineup that included John Mulaney, Stavros Halkias, Fred Armisen and James Austin Johnson on Friday. INsauga reports Saturday's bill was set to feature Adam Ray, Jeff Arcuri and Brad Williams, while Sunday's lineup included Hasan Minhaj, Ronny Chieng and Michael Kosta.

items.title: Stonehooker's Lakeshore Road Restaurant Shuts Down, But Its Beer Store Stays Open
items.summary: According to INsauga, Stonehooker Brewing Co.'s Biergarten CODA restaurant, bar and hospitality operation on Lakeshore Road East closed for good on September 7. The outlet reports the closure ends the space's run as a Mississauga destination for pints, food, live music and events, though the brewery's beer store remains open. INsauga reports Stonehooker's beer also continues to be available at the LCBO, since the retail and hospitality sides of the business are separate. According to the outlet, owner Ross Noel said that distinction matters for customers who may have assumed the closure meant the end of Stonehooker altogether, noting the brand still has value. INsauga reports Stonehooker had announced the hospitality wind-down last month, and the final day included one last celebration for regulars before the doors closed.

items.title: Streetsville Loses Its BeaverTails Outlet as Shelly's Chill Also Shuts Down
items.summary: According to INsauga, the BeaverTails location at 213 Queen Street South in Streetsville has closed, along with Shelly's Chill, which operated in the same space. The outlet reports both businesses are now marked as permanently closed on Google Maps, and the BeaverTails location is no longer listed on the chain's own website. INsauga reports the Streetsville location opened in 2022, offering the chain's signature flat fried dough pastries topped with items like chocolate hazelnut spread, maple spread and crushed Oreo cookies, along with fries, poutine and ice cream. According to the outlet, BeaverTails began as a wooden booth in Ottawa's ByWard Market in 1980 and has since grown to about 50 storefronts and more than 150 mobile locations. INsauga reports Shelly's Chill, which served chicken sandwiches, bowls, shakes and fries at the same address, could not be reached for comment on the closure.

items.title: Council Revisits AI Data Centre Rules One Month Into Its Construction Moratorium
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga city officials are set to revisit the debate over large AI data centres at a general committee meeting on Wednesday, just over a month after imposing a construction moratorium on the facilities. The outlet reports a report from Planning and Building Commissioner Andrew Whittemore outlines the Ontario government's newly released playbook for building such facilities across the province. INsauga reports city council voted unanimously two weeks earlier to impose a moratorium of one to two years on data centre developments to give the city more time to study the issue. According to the outlet, that decision followed roughly two dozen deputations from residents and other stakeholders at a July 29 council meeting, with most speakers opposed to the large new facilities. INsauga reports Whittemore's report notes that significant regulatory and legislative changes would be needed to implement elements of the province's strategy.

items.title: Showing Up Now Counts Toward Grades Under New Ontario High School Rules
items.summary: According to INsauga, a major change to how Ontario high school students are graded takes effect this year as students in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon return to class. The outlet reports the new provincial rules apply to students in Grades 9 through 12 and are being implemented by both the Peel District School Board and the Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board. INsauga reports students in Grades 9 and 10 will now have final marks calculated as 65 per cent classroom work, 20 per cent mandatory final evaluations and 15 per cent attendance and participation. According to the outlet, Grades 11 and 12 students will be graded on 65 per cent classroom work, 25 per cent final evaluations and 10 per cent attendance and participation, meaning showing up to class can now directly affect a student's mark. INsauga reports the province says excused absences, including illness, inclement weather and approved cultural or religious observances, will not count against a student's grade.

items.title: Philippine Festival and Literary Festival Fill Out Mississauga's Sept. 11-13 Weekend
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the city is hosting a slate of cultural festivals this September and October, including the Philippine Festival Mississauga and the Mississauga Literary Festival over the Sept. 11-13 weekend. The outlet reports the Philippine Festival is a three-day celebration hosted in partnership with Culture Philippines Ontario, held at Mississauga Celebration Square with music, dance showcases and traditional cuisine. According to the outlet, a third event originally planned for that weekend, the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival at Erindale Park, was called off just days before it was set to begin. Mississauga.com reports organizers said they are exploring new dates for the comedy festival and will follow up with ticket holders once one is set. According to the outlet, the Portugalo Fest is still set to return to Celebration Square on September 19.
